overview:
This check monitors hardware temperatures and thermal constraints on Windows and macOS hosts.

On Windows, the check collects the temperature and passive performance limit for each thermal zone exposed by the operating system. On macOS, it collects available CPU, GPU, SSD, and battery temperatures from the Apple System Management Controller (AppleSMC), along with the system thermal pressure level.

The check omits sensors that are unavailable on a host instead of reporting them as zero. The set of available metrics can vary by hardware model.

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.82.0 on Windows and 7.84.0 on macOS.
setup:
### Installation

The Thermal integration is included in the [Datadog Agent][1] package. No additional installation is required.

### Configuration

The Thermal check is not enabled by default. To enable it, complete the following steps:

1. Copy the sample [`thermal.d/conf.yaml`][2] to `thermal.d/conf.yaml` in the `conf.d` folder at the root of the Agent's [configuration directory][3]. No check-specific options are required:

   ```yaml
   init_config:

   instances:
     - {}
   ```

2. [Restart the Agent][4].

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][5] and look for `thermal` under the **Checks** section.

On Windows and macOS, the check submits only the thermal metrics exposed by the host. If the host exposes no supported thermal data, as on some virtual machines, the check runs without submitting metrics.

[1]: /account/settings/agent/latest
[2]: https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/cmd/agent/dist/conf.d/thermal.d/conf.yaml.example
[3]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/configuration/agent-configuration-files/#agent-configuration-directory
[4]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-commands/#restart-the-agent

metrics.name: system.thermal.passive_limit
metrics.description: [Windows] The percentage of maximum performance permitted by passive thermal throttling for the thermal zone.

metrics.name: system.thermal.pressure_level
metrics.description: [macOS] The system thermal pressure level: 0 nominal, 1 moderate, 2 heavy, 3 trapping, or 4 sleeping.

metrics.name: system.thermal.temperature
metrics.description: [Windows] The current temperature of the thermal zone.

metrics.name: system.thermal.temperature.battery
metrics.description: [macOS] The highest available battery temperature reported by AppleSMC.

metrics.name: system.thermal.temperature.cpu
metrics.description: [macOS] The highest available CPU temperature reported by AppleSMC.

metrics.name: system.thermal.temperature.gpu
metrics.description: [macOS] The highest available GPU temperature reported by AppleSMC.

metrics.name: system.thermal.temperature.ssd
metrics.description: [macOS] The highest available SSD temperature reported by AppleSMC.
